facts.text: In 1733, 67 landowners formed the Proprietors of Hartland, and the General Court decreed the area 'Hartford land,' later shortened to Hartland.
Captain Thomas Giddings Jr. and his wife Mary Coult became Hartland's first permanent settlers in 1754.
When the Saville Dam was completed in 1940, the town's Hartland Hollow was flooded to create the Barkhamsted Reservoir.
The east branch of the Farmington River bisects Hartland and became the northern section of the Barkhamsted Reservoir after the Saville Dam.
Small Native American bands used Hartland's river valley for summer camps, hunting, and fishing, leaving artifacts that still surface today.
More than 70 percent of Hartland's 15,500 acres are permanently set aside as open space, including state forests and conservation trusts.
